notes:
Summary and account notes:
- Use-case: customer-facing conversational assistant + internal doc search + reranking for claims ingestion. Heavy peak windows (EOD batch ingestion) + steady chat traffic during business hours.
- Latency SLO ask (client phrasing): "sub-100ms for fast replies; <300ms for complex responses; streaming first-byte as low as possible". They keep mixing client-side SDK timings w/ server-side processing times.
- Draft targets we proposed for evaluation POC: non-streaming generation p50=40ms, p95=140ms, p99=400ms (end-to-end server-side). Streaming: first-byte p50=25ms, p95=120ms; end-to-stream p95<=600ms for long responses.
- Key measurement alignment items to resolve: clock sync (NTP), whether measured at SDK (client) vs edge (ingress) vs model host, inclusion/exclusion of network egress to customer client, and how streaming TTFB is reported in SDKs.
- Throughput/Reserved GPU planning: engineering expects 500 concurrent chat sessions (avg 12 tokens/sec per session) with 20% spiky bursts (x2) — translates to ~1200 concurrent effective token streams. They want a 99.9% availability SLA for Dedicated pool.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-high; will accept reserve commit if clear unit economics and fallbacks to cheaper quantized variants for non-critical routes.
- Security: must support customer-managed KMS, VPC peering, and audit logs shipped to SIEM.
- Quote from engineering director on call: "We'll benchmark and sign if Redwood can guarantee p95 under sustained concurrent load + clear measurement semantics."
- Next immediate actions: run capacity workshop with infra, deliver measurement spec (server vs client definitions), update SLA language for data residency.
- Open questions: exact tokenization assumptions for long-form replies, SDK instrumentation method, whether CDN/edge will be used and how that affects observed latencies.
measurement_alignment_notes:
Detailed SLO alignment notes: p50/p95/p99 semantics, streaming vs non-streaming, client-side timing considerations:
- Definitions agreed to propose for POC: p50/p95/p99 measured at Redwood ingress (edge) with server-side processing time included; client-side network RTT excluded unless client requests end-to-end metric.
- Streaming metrics: define TTFB (time-to-first-byte) and TTE (time-to-end). For streaming, primary SLO is TTFB p95 <= 120ms; secondary SLO is TTE p95 <= 600ms for typical 512-token responses.
- Non-streaming metrics: measure server processing from request receive to last token emitted; p95 target 140ms for default prompt template.
- Clock sync & instrumentation: require SDK + server clocks NTP-synced; recommend server-side timestamps be canonical. Add SDK hook to report client RTT for optional end-to-end graphs.
- Measurement granularity: 1s buckets for p50/p95 computation during load tests; longer retention for p99 analysis.
- Fallback behavior: under contention, route to quantized model variant with documented delta in p95 and quality. POC will include A/B traffic split to measure quality/regression.
- Reporting: send token-level cost + latency breakdown per-request to Crimson Quay's Console tenant; exportable CSV for legal review.
sizing_and_throughput_estimate:
Reserved GPU planning summary (POC):
- Baseline workload: 500 concurrent chat sessions, avg 12 tokens/sec, avg response length 220 tokens.
- Peak burst: 2x for 15% of windows -> plan for 1200 concurrent effective token streams.
- Suggested Dedicated pool: 16x A100-equivalent GPUs (quantization-friendly kernels) with autoscale headroom of +4 GPUs for bursts.
- Expected throughput: ~8500 tokens/sec sustained; with batching and KV cache, average per-GPU throughput increases ~1.8x.
- SLA ask: 99.9% uptime for Dedicated pool, p95 latency guarantees per route; include fallback routing policy to hosted-compatible model when capacity exhausted.
